title: Copilot connectors vs Power Platform connectors

sentences.text: Monday at Contoso.
Marta asks Nexo two kinds of questions.
What does this H R policy say?
And how many units of a product are in the warehouse right now?
Valeria, the developer, has to give Nexo both answers.
The policies hardly change.
The inventory changes every minute.
By the end of this class you will know which family of connectors serves each question, and why.

scenes.title: A library and a phone call

sentences.text: Here is the picture to keep.
Two families of connectors give an agent knowledge about your company.
Think of a library and a phone call.
In the library, someone copied the books into a catalog, so you can search them fast.
On the phone call, you ask the data owner right then.
Each one serves a different purpose, and the exam checks that you know which is which.
First family: Copilot connectors.
A Copilot connector copies, or indexes, the content of an external system into Microsoft Graph.
It respects the permissions of the source, called the A C L, so each person only sees what they could already see.
It gives semantic indexing and citations.
The tenant admin sets it up, and it is reused in Copilot and in Microsoft Search.
This model is called index then answer.
Second family: Power Platform connectors.
In real-time knowledge mode, which is in preview, each question runs against the source system with the identity of the user.
The data is not copied or moved.
Only metadata is indexed, such as table and column names, so the agent knows what it can ask.
That is the phone call: Nexo dials the system at the moment Marta asks.
Your turn.
Contoso's warehouse inventory changes every minute.
The data owner does not want the stock copied.
Which option should Valeria give Nexo?
A Copilot connector that indexes the stock?
A Power Platform connector in real-time mode?
Or a Copilot connector shared with Microsoft Search?
Decide before I answer.
A Power Platform connector in real-time mode.
Each question goes live to the system with the identity of the user, and nothing is copied.
A Copilot connector indexes the stock into Microsoft Graph, the copy the owner refused.
So how do you choose?
Ask one question about the source: does it change little, or every minute?
If the content hardly changes, like manuals or policies, use Copilot connectors.
If the data changes every minute and should not be replicated, like an inventory, use Power Platform connectors.
And you do not have to pick only one.
There is also a mixed mode, which uses each family where it fits.
Watch Contoso do it.
The product manuals and the H R policies hardly change, so they are indexed with a Copilot connector, and Nexo answers with citations.
The warehouse inventory changes every minute and must not be copied, so Valeria uses a Power Platform connector with real-time knowledge.
Each query goes to the system with the identity of the person asking.
Nexo combines both in mixed mode.
Your turn.
Marta asks about H R policies.
The manager wants citations, and each employee sees only what they could already see.
Which option fits these policies?
A Copilot connector set up by the admin?
A Power Platform connector asked live?
Or indexing only the table and column names?
Decide before I answer.
A Copilot connector, set up by the tenant admin.
It indexes the policies, respects the A C L, and gives citations.
A live query is meant for data that changes every minute, not stable policies.
One practical detail, and the exam likes to ask about it.
Valeria is ready to publish Nexo to channels.
Because Nexo uses Copilot connectors, authentication needs one scope: External Item dot Read dot All.
Valeria adds it in authentication before she publishes.
The trap on the exam is simply forgetting this scope.
Remember why it is there: the Copilot connectors, not the real-time Power Platform connectors.
Your turn.
Valeria publishes Nexo to channels.
Nexo uses a Copilot connector for the manuals and the H R policies.
What does authentication need?
The identity of each user, asked live?
A scope for the Power Platform connector?
Or the External Item Read All scope?
Decide before I answer.
The External Item dot Read dot All scope.
Publishing to channels with Copilot connectors needs that scope in authentication.
The Power Platform connector is not the reason for it, and forgetting this scope is the trap the exam sets.
Here are the steps.
Open your agent in Copilot Studio and go to the Knowledge tab.
Select Add knowledge and look at the list of available connectors.
Ask yourself if the source changes little or every minute.
If it is stable and you want citations, choose a Copilot connector, which the tenant admin enables.
If you need the data by the minute, choose a Power Platform connector with real-time knowledge.
When publishing to channels with Copilot connectors, add the External Item dot Read dot All scope in authentication.
Back to Contoso.
Marta asks about an H R policy, and Nexo answers from the index, with a citation.
She asks about the stock, and Nexo makes the live call with her identity.
Remember for the exam: stable content with citations, Copilot connectors.
Data by the minute without copying it, real-time knowledge with Power Platform connectors.
And the External Item dot Read dot All scope when you publish.
Next, Azure A I Search as knowledge.
